learning_outcomes.objective: Identify the subatomic particles: protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Explain J.J. Thomson's, Rutherford's, and Bohr's models of the atom.
Calculate the atomic number and mass number.
Draw the electron distribution for the first 18 elements.

ai_context.learning_goal: Student should master the arrangement of subatomic particles and be able to draw atomic structures.
common_misconceptions: Electrons crash into the nucleus (Rutherford's flaw).
Isotopes have different chemical properties (they don't, they only have different physical properties like mass).
Neutrons have a charge (they are neutral).
ai_context.tutor_hint: If the student struggles with electron distribution, ask them to think of the shells as a stadium seating arrangement: the first row (K shell) can only fit 2 people, the second row (L shell) can fit 8.
